title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: no one foreseen persevering to whom God has not yet decreed the gift
latin: Octavo, sic argumentamur. Nemo unquam praevisus est ut habens fidem perseverantem, cui Deus nondum decrevit hoc eximium donum impertire. Quod si Deus jam decreverit Petro, Paulo, aut cuilibet homini singulari dare perseverantiam; manifestum est illum jam esse a Deo ad vitam electum et ordinatum. Nam in ipso perseverantiae dono sita est infallibilis ad vitam aeternam ordinatio. Parum igitur rationi consentaneum est, ipsum Deum eligere singulares personas ad vitam ex praevisione proprii sui doni, quod nunquam dedit, aut dare decrevit, nisi illis quos antecedenter ad vitam aeternam destinavit.
pass_a: Eighthly, we argue thus. No one was ever foreseen as having persevering faith, to whom God has not yet decreed to impart this excellent gift. But if God has already decreed to give perseverance to Peter, Paul, or any singular man; it is manifest that he is already elected and ordained by God to life. For in the very gift of perseverance is situated an infallible ordination to eternal life. Little therefore is it agreeable to reason that God himself should elect singular persons to life from foresight of his own gift, which he never gave, or decreed to give, except to those whom he antecedently destined to eternal life.
pass_b: Eighth argument: no one was ever foreseen as having persevering faith unless God had already decreed to give that excellent gift. If God has decreed perseverance for Peter, Paul, or any particular person, that one is already elected and ordained to life — for the gift of perseverance itself carries an infallible ordination to eternal life. It is hardly reasonable that God should elect particular persons to life by foresight of his own gift, which he never gives or decrees to give except to those he has already destined to eternal life.

lemmas.gloss: no one foreseen persevering without the decreed gift
ordination to life sits in the gift itself

title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: first — perseverance from God's gift (Jer. 32:40; 2 Thess. 3:3), not bare free choice
latin: Nihil video in hoc argumento quod ullo modo possit labefactari aut in dubium vocari. Nam primo, si quis diceret fidem perseverantem posse in aliquibus praevideri quibus Deus hanc perseverantiam nondum decreverit donare, ille tantum bonum ab humano arbitrio, non a Divino munere arcesseret. At tota Scriptura reclamat, quae perseverantiam sanctorum ex dono Dei ostendit dimanare: Reverentiam mei indam animo ipsorum, ut non recedant a me, Jer. xxxii. 40. 2 Thess. iii. 3. Fidelis est Deus, qui stabiliet vos et tuebitur a malo. Et Augustinus secundum Scripturas clare docuit, hanc perseverandi possibilitatem et voluntatem Divinae gratiae largitate donari sanctis in regnum Dei praedestinatis, aliis non donari. Est ergo verissimum illud Aquinatis: Voluntas Dei qua vult hoc bonum alicui diligendo, est causa quod illud bonum ab eo prae aliis habeatur, Part. 1. qu. 23. art. 4.
pass_a: I see nothing in this argument that can in any way be shaken or called into doubt. For first, if anyone should say that persevering faith can be foreseen in some to whom God has not yet decreed to give this perseverance, he would fetch so great a good from human choice, not from the Divine gift. But the whole Scripture protests, which shows the perseverance of the saints to flow from the gift of God: I will put my fear in their heart, that they may not depart from me, Jer. 32:40. 2 Thess. 3:3: Faithful is God, who will establish you and keep you from evil. And Augustine according to the Scriptures clearly taught that this possibility and will of persevering is given by the largess of Divine grace to the saints predestined into the kingdom of God, and not given to others. Therefore that of Aquinas is most true: The will of God by which he wills this good to someone in loving him is the cause that that good is had by him before others, Part 1, q. 23, art. 4.
pass_b: Nothing here can be shaken. First: if persevering faith could be foreseen in those to whom God has not yet decreed perseverance, that great good would come from human choice, not God's gift. All Scripture protests — saints' perseverance flows from God's gift: I will put my fear in their heart, that they may not depart from me (Jer. 32:40); Faithful is God, who will establish you and keep you from evil (2 Thess. 3:3). Augustine, following Scripture, taught that the power and will to persevere is given by grace's largess to saints predestined into God's kingdom — and not to others. So Aquinas is right: God's loving will that someone have this good is why he has it before others (ST 1.23.4).

lemmas.gloss: God's will cause of the good before others

title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: second — efficacious means only from intention of the end; 1 Pet. 1:5
latin: Secundo, perseverantiam non donari aut destinari nisi ad vitam aeternam electo et destinato, inde clarum est, quod ab agente qui vim et efficaciam mediorum intelligit, media ad finem consequendum infallibiliter efficacia nunquam praeparantur et donantur cuiquam nisi ex proposito et desiderio finis. Huc spectant illa Petri verba, virtute Dei custodimini per fidem ad salutem, 1 Petr. i. 5. Deus inspirat fidem cordibus nostris, inspiratam custodit ne exstinguatur, atque idcirco hoc facit, ut per fidem perducamur ad salutem. Salus igitur eorum omnium fuit apud Deum certissima, quibus fidem perseverantem dare decrevit.
pass_a: Secondly, that perseverance is not given or destined except to one elected and destined to eternal life is clear from this, that by an agent who understands the force and efficacy of means, means infallibly efficacious for obtaining the end are never prepared and given to anyone except from the purpose and desire of the end. Hither look those words of Peter: by the power of God you are kept through faith unto salvation, 1 Pet. 1:5. God inspires faith into our hearts, keeps what is inspired lest it be extinguished, and therefore does this, that through faith we may be led to salvation. The salvation therefore of all those to whom he decreed to give persevering faith was most certain with God.
pass_b: Second: perseverance is given only to one already elected and destined to eternal life. An agent who knows what means can do never prepares and gives infallibly efficacious means except from purpose and desire of the end. So Peter: by God's power you are kept through faith unto salvation (1 Pet. 1:5). God inspires faith, keeps it from going out, and does so that through faith we may be led to salvation. All to whom he decreed persevering faith had salvation most certain with God.

lemmas.gloss: infallible means only from desire of the end

title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: Arminians twist the gift — sufficient grace to persevere if they will
latin: Hoc argumentum valde torquet tam Arminianos quam Jesuitas. Arminiani itaque non ausint aperte negare, fidem perseverantem esse donum Dei, tamen strenue negant, actionem eam per quam Deus nobis fidem donat, semper efficacem, certam, et invictam esse. Atque porro docent, quando Deus dat hominibus potentiam ad ipsum perveniendi, fidem jam esse iisdem paratam ut donum, modo continuetur haec gratia. Proculdubio idem sentiunt de perseverantia, nempe hoc dono nil aliud designari quam illam sufficientem gratiam, qua datur hominibus potentia perseverandi si velint. Tale autem donum non arguit praeeuntem destinationem ad vitam aeternam; quia hoc modo fides et perseverantia donatur illis, qui nec fidem, nec perseverantiam, nec vitam aeternam unquam habuerunt aut habituri sunt.
pass_a: This argument greatly tortures both Arminians and Jesuits. The Arminians therefore would not dare openly to deny that persevering faith is the gift of God, yet they strenuously deny that that action by which God gives us faith is always efficacious, certain, and invincible. And further they teach that when God gives men the power of arriving at him, faith is already prepared for them as a gift, provided this grace be continued. Without doubt they think the same of perseverance, namely that by this gift nothing else is designated than that sufficient grace by which power is given to men of persevering if they will. But such a gift does not argue a preceding destination to eternal life; because in this way faith and perseverance is given to those who never had, nor will have, either faith, or perseverance, or eternal life.
pass_b: This argument badly torments Arminians and Jesuits alike. Arminians dare not openly deny that persevering faith is God's gift — yet they strongly deny that the act by which God gives faith is always efficacious, certain, and invincible. They teach that when God gives men power to reach him, faith is already prepared as a gift if that grace continues. Doubtless they hold the same of perseverance: the 'gift' means only sufficient grace — power to persevere if they will. That kind of gift does not imply prior destination to eternal life; it is 'given' even to those who never had and never will have faith, perseverance, or eternal life.

lemmas.gloss: power to persevere if they will

title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: gift implies reception — Phil. 1:29; Augustine De corr. et grat.
latin: Sed haec parum coherent aut inter se aut cum Scripturis. Non inter se; quia fides aut perseverantia data singulari personae ex parte Dei, innuit obtentam et habitam ex parte hominis. Quaedam enim dona ejusmodi sunt, ut involvant ipsam receptionem, absque qua ne intelligi quidem possunt esse donata. Tale donum est bona voluntas credentis et perseverantis, quae nunquam fuit a Deo data ulli homini a quo non fuit accepta. Non enim quaeritur de dono parato et offerendo, atque sub conditione contingente dando certis personis, aut non dando, sed de dono certis personis vere et actualiter donato. Porro, cum Scripturis pugnat Arminiana illa fidei ac perseverantiae donatae interpretatio. Nam Scripturae dicunt fidem iis donatam quibus datum est ipsum credere, non quibus datum est solummodo ut possint credere, Phil. i. 29. Perseverantiam etiam illis datam pronunciant, non qui potuerunt perseverare et resilierunt, sed qui Divino munere ita corroborati et sustentati fuerint, ut ipso facto perseveraverint. Late hoc probat Augustinus, De Corr. et grat. cap. 11, 12. Ubi ostendit, dari jam omnibus praedestinatis in Christo, quod non fuit datum Adamo; nempe tale adjutorium, ut per illud non solummodo perseverare possint si velint, sed etiam ut velint, et reapse perseverent.
pass_a: But these things cohere little either among themselves or with the Scriptures. Not among themselves; because faith or perseverance given to a singular person on God's part hints that it is obtained and had on man's part. For certain gifts are of such a kind that they involve the very reception, without which they cannot even be understood to have been given. Such a gift is the good will of the believer and perseverer, which was never given by God to any man by whom it was not accepted. For the question is not of a gift prepared and to be offered, and under a contingent condition to be given to certain persons, or not given, but of a gift truly and actually given to certain persons. Further, that Arminian interpretation of faith and perseverance given fights with the Scriptures. For the Scriptures say faith is given to those to whom it is given to believe itself, not to those to whom it is given only that they may be able to believe, Phil. 1:29. They also pronounce perseverance given to those, not who could persevere and sprang back, but who by the Divine gift were so strengthened and sustained that in very fact they persevered. Augustine proves this at large, On Rebuke and Grace, chapters 11, 12. Where he shows that there is now given to all predestined in Christ what was not given to Adam; namely such a help, that by it they may not only be able to persevere if they will, but also that they may will, and in very deed persevere.
pass_b: This coheres neither with itself nor with Scripture. A faith or perseverance God gives to a particular person implies it is had on man's side. Some gifts include the reception itself — without reception they cannot even be understood as given. The good will of the believer and perseverer is such a gift: God never gave it to anyone who did not receive it. The question is not a gift prepared and offered under a contingent condition, but a gift truly and actually given to certain persons. Arminian reading fights Scripture: faith is given to those to whom it is given to believe — not merely to be able to believe (Phil. 1:29). Perseverance is pronounced given not to those who could have persevered and sprang back, but to those so strengthened by God's gift that they actually persevered. Augustine at length (On Rebuke and Grace 11–12): all predestined in Christ receive what Adam did not — help such that they not only can persevere if they will, but will, and in fact persevere.

lemmas.gloss: given to believe, not merely able to believe
help so they will and actually persevere

title: Cap. VI Arg. 8 close: Vasquez split grace/glory fails — will to give the kingdom causes perseverance
latin: Ab hoc dono, quibusdam specialiter praeparato et donato, nos colligimus, vitam aeternam fuisse iisdem antecedenter destinatam. Vasques Jesuita convictus de absoluta hac et gratuita certarum personarum ad fidem et perseverantiam praedestinatione, respondet, esse verissimum, praedestinationem ad habendam gratiam non dependere ex praevisis meritis aut actionibus nostris; sed electionem ad habendam gloriam ex illis dependere, atque hanc esse perpetuam Scripturarum et Augustini sententiam. Sed frustra conatur Jesuita divellere, quae Scriptura et Augustinus optimus hac in re Scripturarum interpres, docuit esse conjunctissima. Scriptura enim non agnoscit aliam electionem aut praedestinationem ad gratiam efficacem, quam quae connexa est cum ea voluntate dandi gloriam; quae voluntas, secundum nostrum considerandi modum, prior est voluntate dandi gratiam efficacem, et causa ac regula ejusdem. Hinc praedestinati dicimur in adoptionem filiorum, Ephes. i. 5. quae non modo gratiae, sed gloriae sive haereditatis caelestis destinationem perspicue denotat. Sic Christus loquens de praedestinatis, Luc. xii. 32. Nolite, inquit, timere, pusille grex, quia complacuit Patri vestro dare vobis regnum. Ubi voluntas dandi regnum affertur tanquam causa peculiaris ejus providentiae quam Deus exercet erga electos, ut eos custodiat, et non obstantibus periculis et tentationibus perseverare faciat. Voluntas ergo dandi gloriam, sive electio ad vitam, est ratio cur prae aliis perseverent; non praevisa perseverantia, ratio cur prae aliis electi fuerint.
pass_a: From this gift, specially prepared and given to certain ones, we gather that eternal life was antecedently destined for the same. Vasquez the Jesuit, convicted concerning this absolute and gratuitous predestination of certain persons to faith and perseverance, replies that it is most true that predestination to the having of grace does not depend from foresighted merits or our actions; but that election to the having of glory depends from those, and that this is the perpetual sentence of the Scriptures and of Augustine. But in vain does the Jesuit try to tear apart what Scripture and Augustine, the best interpreter of the Scriptures in this matter, taught to be most closely joined. For Scripture does not acknowledge another election or predestination to efficacious grace than that which is connected with that will of giving glory; which will, according to our mode of considering, is prior to the will of giving efficacious grace, and the cause and rule of the same. Hence we are said to be predestinated unto the adoption of sons, Eph. 1:5, which clearly denotes destination not only of grace, but of glory or the heavenly inheritance. So Christ speaking of the predestinated, Luke 12:32: Fear not, little flock, for it has pleased your Father to give you the kingdom. Where the will of giving the kingdom is brought as the peculiar cause of that providence which God exercises toward the elect, that he may keep them, and make them persevere notwithstanding dangers and temptations. The will therefore of giving glory, or election to life, is the reason why they persevere before others; not foresighted perseverance the reason why they were elected before others.
pass_b: From this gift specially prepared and given to some, we gather eternal life was already destined for them. Vasquez the Jesuit, pressed by this absolute gratuitous predestination of certain persons to faith and perseverance, answers: yes, predestination to grace does not hang on foresighted merits — but election to glory does, and that is the standing view of Scripture and Augustine. In vain he tries to split what Scripture and Augustine join most closely. Scripture knows no election to efficacious grace except what is tied to the will to give glory — which will, in our way of considering, is prior to the will to give efficacious grace, and its cause and rule. Hence we are predestined unto adoption as sons (Eph. 1:5) — destination of glory and the heavenly inheritance, not grace alone. So Christ to the predestined (Luke 12:32): Fear not, little flock, for it pleased your Father to give you the kingdom — the will to give the kingdom as the peculiar cause of the providence that keeps the elect and makes them persevere through dangers. The will to give glory (election to life) is why they persevere before others — not foresighted perseverance why they were elected before others.

lemmas.gloss: splits predestination to grace from election to glory
will to give the kingdom causes perseverance
